description: The village-state save mapping (Features WV1, P1.core; CROSS-ENGINE-FEATURES §4, 1. Saves): GameSaveState in, SaveFile currentState and conversations out, and back. The tutorial's progress rides in the registered currentState.extensions.tutorial (PL.tutorial-progress-save; contract.tutorialRule). The puzzle, platformer and strategy runs ride in the registered currentState.extensions.puzzle, .platformer and .strategy (P9j.core; contract.puzzleRule, contract.platformerRule, contract.strategyRule). It adds no new SaveFile field and no unregistered extension. The villagers ride in core's registered currentState.extensions.aiBlackboards, one board per villager keyed by its world-scoped CURIE, and the writer stamps its runtime and position frame on the player agent's board. The sky rides in the registered currentState.extensions.weather (the weather director's serialize() and the surface wetness; contract.weatherRule), the survival needs in the registered currentState.extensions.survivalNeeds (contract.survivalRule), what was gathered and produced in the registered currentState.extensions.gathering (contract.gatheringRule), where the playthrough has been and how it travels in the registered currentState.extensions.traversal (contract.traversalRule), the player's relationships, romances, reputation, what NPCs remember of the player and NPC volition in the registered currentState.extensions.social (contract.socialRule), the player's language learning (the language book, collected words, naming and identification) in the registered currentState.extensions.languageLearning (contract.languageRule), and the villagers' day in the registered currentState.extensions.npcLife (contract.npcLifeRule). The per-conversation records (gameState.conversations) fold into SaveFile.conversations, one row per NPC, and a load splits each row back into one record per conversation; every timestamp is the wall-clock instant the host supplies, never play time (PL.core-save-conversations-projection; contract.conversationsRule, contract.conversationClockRule). A save written by any engine loads in the others. Runner: src/save-file-game-state-corpus.ts (ops write, read, roundTrip, stamp, agentCurie, timeStateOf, totalHoursOf, conversationTimestamp, conversationEpochMs, skillKb). write, read and roundTrip are the checked entry points (writeVillageSave, readVillageSave) and refuse by code and field. Numbers compare within tolerance; everything else exactly, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent). Regenerate with npm run village-state-corpus; npm run village-state-corpus:check fails on any difference.

contract.weatherRule: gameState.weather = {director: WeatherDirector.serialize() (null before the first roll), surfaceWetness: 0..1 or null}. Written to currentState.extensions.weather with only those keys (director: day, season, condition), replacing the stored block; a game state with no weather (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back with both keys (a missing surfaceWetness is null); an absent or null block reads as no weather key, and the host restores the director's default. Readable: an object whose director is null or {day: whole number >= 0, season: string|null, condition: string|null} and whose surfaceWetness is absent, null or a number in 0..1. Otherwise unreadable_weather, keys = the unreadable members in ascending order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.survivalRule: gameState.survival = survivalSaveBlock(): {readings: {<need id>: finite number}, modifiers: [{id: string, needType: string, rateMultiplier: finite >= 0, remainingMs: finite or null (permanent), source: string}]}. Written to currentState.extensions.survivalNeeds with only those members (a missing modifiers list is written empty, a missing source as ''), replacing the stored block; a game state with no survival (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no survival key, and each need starts at its start value. Readable: an object whose readings is an object of finite numbers and whose modifiers is absent or a list of such rows. Otherwise unreadable_survival, keys = the unreadable members (readings, readings.<id>, modifiers, modifiers[<i>]) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.gatheringRule: gameState.gathering = gatheringSaveBlock(): {nodes: [{id: string, remaining: finite >= 0, respawnInMs: finite >= 0 or null}], actions: {<actor>: {<action>: finite >= 0}}, production: null or {plots: [[plot, crop, plantedDay, waterings]], spots: [[spot, castsLeft]], veins: [[vein, swingsLeft]], carried: [[actor, [[item, qty]]]], day}, business: null or {businesses: [{id, type, owner: string, settlement?: string, foundedDay: finite, closedDay?: finite, capital: finite, arrears: finite >= 0, shut: boolean, staff: [[person, role]]}], purses: [[actor, coin]], day: the last day settled}}. Written to currentState.extensions.gathering with only those members (missing nodes written [], missing actions {}, missing production or business null, a missing respawnInMs null, a production or business state's missing lists [] and day 0, settlement and closedDay only where set), replacing the stored block; a game state with no gathering (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no gathering key, and every node starts full and every plot empty. Otherwise unreadable_gathering, keys = the unreadable members (nodes, nodes[<i>], actions, actions.<actor>, actions.<actor>.<action>, production, production.plots|spots|veins|carried, production.<list>[<i>], production.day, business, business.businesses|purses, business.<list>[<i>], business.day) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.traversalRule: gameState.traversal = traversalSaveBlock(): {planner: null or {actors: [{id: string, location: string, modes: [string], lent?: {<mode held>: [lender, at least one]}}], blocked: [{from: string, to: string}]}, vehicles: null or {vehicles: [{id: string, location: string, occupants: [string], owner?: string, driver?: string (one of the occupants)}]}, fastTravel: null or {discovered: [string], journeys: whole >= 0}, riding: {<actor>: <kind>}}. Written to currentState.extensions.traversal with only those members and each row with only its keys (a missing modes written [walk], lent only when it names a mode (keys and lenders sorted), a missing occupants [], an owner or driver only when set, missing lists [], a missing journeys 0, a missing director null, a missing riding {}), replacing the stored block; a game state with no traversal (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no traversal key, and everyone starts where the world places them, nothing found, on foot. Otherwise unreadable_traversal, keys = the unreadable members (planner, planner.actors|blocked, planner.<list>[<i>], vehicles, vehicles.vehicles, vehicles.vehicles[<i>], fastTravel, fastTravel.discovered, fastTravel.journeys, riding, riding.<actor>) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.socialRule: gameState.social = socialSaveBlock(): {relationships: {<npc>: integer -1000..1000}, romance: null or {timestep: whole >= 0, tracks: [{npcId, npcName, stage: string, spark: whole 0..1000, lastInteraction, totalInteractions, giftsGiven, datesCompleted, rejectionCooldown: whole >= 0, rejected: boolean}]}, reputation: null or {entries: [{entityType, entityId, entityName: string, score: integer -100..100, isBanned: boolean, banExpiryMs: integer or null, violationCount, outstandingFines: whole >= 0}]}, memory: {<npc>: {quests: {<quest>: assigned|completed|failed|abandoned}, conversations: whole >= 0}}, volition: null or {agents: [{agent: string, motives, appeals: {<id>: number}, spent: [string]}], pairs: [{agent, other: string, spark: integer 0..100, status: string or null}]}}. Written to currentState.extensions.social with only those members and each row with only its keys (missing maps written {}, a missing romance, reputation or volition null, a missing timestep 0, missing lists []), replacing the stored block; a game state with no social block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no social key, and every NPC is a stranger. The legacy currentState.npcs.relationships, npcs.romance and reputation are carried untouched. Otherwise unreadable_social, keys = the unreadable members (relationships, relationships.<npc>, romance, romance.timestep, romance.tracks, romance.tracks[<i>] (a second track for one NPC too), reputation, reputation.entries, reputation.entries[<i>] (a second entry for one entity too), memory, memory.<npc>, volition, volition.agents|pairs, volition.<list>[<i>]) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.languageRule: gameState.languageLearning = languageSaveBlock(): {book: null or {language: string, clockMs: whole, fluency: integer 0..100000 (thousandths of a point), cefr: A1|A2|B1|B2|C1|C2 or null, conversations, correctUsages: whole, words: [{word: trimmed non-empty string, language, meaning: string, category, context: string or null, encountered, correct, incorrect, halves, last: whole, types: {<active_use|passive_hover|passive_read|quiz_correct|quiz_incorrect>: positive whole}}], grammar: [{pattern: string, correct, incorrect: whole, mastered: boolean, examples, explanations: [string]}]}, collected: [string], naming: {<id>: {attempts: whole, named: boolean}}, identification: {<id>: {attempts: whole, identified: boolean, bestScore: integer 0..100}}}. A word's types sum to encountered, weigh (2, 1, 1, 2, 0 halves) to halves, its active uses and right answers are correct and its wrong answers incorrect. Written to currentState.extensions.languageLearning with only those members and each row with only its keys (a missing book field written as the empty book's: language target, numbers 0, cefr null; missing lists [] and maps {}; a missing book null), replacing the stored block; a game state with no language block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no languageLearning key, and the learner knows no word. The legacy languageProgress, languageProgressDetailed and player.cefrLevel are carried untouched. Otherwise unreadable_language, keys = the unreadable members (book, book.<field>, book.words|grammar, book.words[<i>] (a second row for one word in one language, ignoring case, too), book.grammar[<i>] (a second row for one pattern too), collected, collected[<i>] (a repeat too), naming, naming.<id>, identification, identification.<id>) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.npcLifeRule: gameState.npcLife = npcLifeSaveBlock(): {routines: null or {agents: [{agent: string, routine: string|null, adopted: null or {goal: string, priority: number}, suspension: null or {reason: string, block: string|null, goal: string|null}, resuming?: true}]}, locomotion: null or {actors: [{actor: string, destination: string|null, failures: whole >= 0}]}, planner: null or {cursors: {<agent>: {plan: {agent, goal: string, tick: integer, steps: [{index: whole, action, target, achieves: string, utility: number, takeableNow: boolean}], complete: boolean, stoppedBy: satisfied|step-ceiling|expansion-ceiling|no-step, unmet: [string], expansions: whole}, stepIndex: whole <= steps, interrupted: null|goal-satisfied|goal-abandoned|step-forbidden|step-blocked|external}}}, escorts: [{npcId, questId, objectiveId: string, destination: {x, z: integer mm}, radiusMm: whole or null}], posts: [{npcId, questId: string, hold: {npcId (the post's own), at, face: {x, z: integer mm}, pose: idle|interact|talk|sit, why: string, untilMs: whole or null}}], movers: {<npc>: {current: null or command, queue: [command], conversation: null or {face: point, saved: null or command, savedQueue: [command]}, snags: whole, draws: whole}} with command = {target: point, speed: stroll|walk|hurry, enter?: true}}. Written to currentState.extensions.npcLife with only those members and each row with only its keys (resuming and enter only when true; a missing nullable written null, a missing count 0, a missing list [], missing cursors or movers {}, a missing layer null; cursors and movers in id order), replacing the stored block; a game state with no NPC life (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no npcLife key, and every villager starts its day afresh. Otherwise unreadable_npc_life, keys = the unreadable members (routines, routines.agents, routines.agents[<i>], locomotion, locomotion.actors, locomotion.actors[<i>], planner, planner.cursors, planner.cursors.<agent>, escorts, escorts[<i>], posts, posts[<i>], movers, movers.<npc>) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.progressionRule: gameState.progression = progressionSaveBlock(): {gamification: null or {xp: whole, unlocked: {<one of progressionAchievements>: integer ms}, daily: null or {dateKey: a real YYYY-MM-DD, progress: whole, completed: boolean, true exactly when progress reaches the date's template target}, consecutiveDays, dailyStreak: whole, lastDailyDate: a real YYYY-MM-DD or null (null exactly when dailyStreak is 0), counters: {<one of progressionCounters>: whole}}, skills: null or {actors: [{id: non-empty string, unique, levels, xp, points: {<id>: whole}, unlocked: [non-empty string, no repeat]}]}}. Written to currentState.extensions.progression with only those members and each row with only its keys (unlocked in progressionAchievements order, all ten counters in progressionCounters order (a missing one 0), a missing field as the empty tracker's (0, {}, null); actors by id, their maps by key and unlocked sorted; a missing map {} and unlocked []; a missing member null), replacing the stored block; a game state with no progression block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no progression key, and the player has no XP and no skills. The legacy gamification, achievements and skillTree extensions are carried untouched. Otherwise unreadable_progression, keys = the unreadable members (gamification, gamification.<field>, gamification.unlocked.<id>, gamification.counters.<key>, gamification.daily, gamification.dailyStreak (a streak and a last day that disagree too), skills, skills.actors, skills.actors[<i>] (a repeated id too)) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.tutorialRule: gameState.tutorial = TutorialQuestSystem.saveProgress() / OnboardingManager.saveProgress(): {completed: [objective id], skipped: [objective id], current: objective id or null (the tutorial is over), endedBySkip: boolean}. Written to currentState.extensions.tutorial with only those members (a missing list written [], a missing endedBySkip false; lists in the order given), replacing the stored block; a game state with no tutorial (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block (a new game's save, or one written before the block; the SaveFile version did not move) reads as no tutorial key, and the tutorial starts fresh. Readable: an object whose completed and skipped are absent or lists of non-empty ids with no repeat and no id in both, whose current is present and null or a non-empty id in neither list, and whose endedBySkip is absent or a boolean, true only when current is null and skipped names an objective. Otherwise unreadable_tutorial, keys = the unreadable members (completed, completed[<i>], skipped, skipped[<i>], current, endedBySkip) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.puzzleRule: gameState.puzzle = PuzzleDirector.serialize(): {actors: [{actor: non-empty id, unique, clues, solved, opened, taken: [non-empty id, no repeat], attempts: [[riddle id, wrong answers >= 1]] (no riddle twice, none solved)}]}. Written to currentState.extensions.puzzle with only that member and each row with only its keys (a missing list written []; rows by actor, every list and the attempts in canonical (code-unit) order), replacing the stored block; a game state with no puzzle block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no puzzle key, and the puzzle run starts fresh. Otherwise unreadable_puzzle, keys = the unreadable members (actors, actors[<i>] (a repeated actor too), actors[<i>].clues|solved|opened|taken, actors[<i>].attempts) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.platformerRule: gameState.platformer = PlatformerDirector.serialize(): {runners: [{runner: non-empty id, unique, level: level id or null (between runs), location: a place, or '' only between runs, runCost: whole, checkpoints: [whole >= 1, no repeat; empty between runs], cleared: [[level id, stars 1..3]] (no level twice)}]}. Written to currentState.extensions.platformer with only that member and each row with only its keys (a missing level null, location '', runCost 0, list []; rows by runner, checkpoints ascending, clears by level), replacing the stored block; a game state with no platformer block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no platformer key, and the course starts fresh. Otherwise unreadable_platformer, keys = the unreadable members (runners, runners[<i>] (a repeated runner too), runners[<i>].level|location|runCost|checkpoints|cleared) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.strategyRule: gameState.strategy = StrategyDirector.serialize(): {turn: whole, holders: [[business, faction]] (no business twice), stock: [[faction, resource, amount >= 1]] (zero is absence; no faction's resource twice), workers: [[worker, business]] (no worker twice; the business somebody holds)}. Written to currentState.extensions.strategy with only those members (a missing turn 0, a missing list []; holders by business, stock by faction then resource, workers by worker), replacing the stored block; a game state with no strategy block (absent or null) carries the stored block untouched. Read back as written; an absent or null block reads as no strategy key, and the campaign starts fresh. Otherwise unreadable_strategy, keys = the unreadable members (turn, holders, stock, workers, holders[<i>], stock[<i>], workers[<i>]) in ascending string order (empty when the block is not an object).
contract.conversationsRule: gameState.conversations = [{npcId: non-empty string, npcName: string, timestamp: string (contract.conversationClockRule), turnCount, wordsUsed: [string] (absent: []), targetLanguagePercent, fluencyGained, lines: [{role: player|npc, content: string}] (absent: [])}], one record per conversation, oldest first. WRITE (conversationRowsOf): a record with no line projects nothing (no row made, none touched). The records with lines, in the order listed, are grouped by npcId; each line becomes {role, content, timestamp: its record's}, and an NPC's fresh lines are its records' lines in that order (a tie between timestamps keeps it; nothing is reordered). Each NPC's row is the first stored row whose npcCharacterId is that NPC (a later one is carried untouched); an NPC with none gets a new row with conversationRowKeys (compressedHistory, lastLocationId, lastLocationName null, lists []), appended after every stored row, NPCs in the order of their first record with a line. Of the fresh lines, only those after the longest prefix the row's readable turns ({role: player|npc, content: string, timestamp: string}) end with (role, content and timestamp equal) are appended, after every turn the row held; so writing twice, or saving a load again, adds nothing. totalTurnCount += the lines appended, player's and NPC's alike (a stored count that is not a whole number 0 or more, missing, a string, negative or fractional, reads 0; the row is never refused for it); records' turnCount, targetLanguagePercent and fluencyGained are not projected. npcCharacterName = the last listed non-empty npcName, else the row's ('' for none). wordsUsed = the row's strings, then the NPC's records' words not yet in it, first seen first. Every other key of the row is carried; rows no record with a line names, and rows with no npcCharacterId, are carried untouched in place. A game state with no conversations (absent or null) carries the stored rows untouched. READ (conversationRecordsOf): the first row per non-empty npcCharacterId, its readable turns only; each run of consecutive turns with equal timestamps is one record {npcId, npcName: the row's ('' for none), timestamp, turnCount: the run's player lines, wordsUsed: [] (the row's strings on its last record), targetLanguagePercent: 0, fluencyGained: 0, lines}; rows in order, runs in order. Two conversations with one NPC at the same instant, listed together, read back as one. No readable turn anywhere: no conversations key. The stored rows are never refused. Readable records: otherwise unreadable_conversations at gameState.conversations, keys = [<i>] (not an object), [<i>].npcId, [<i>].npcName, [<i>].timestamp, [<i>].wordsUsed, [<i>].lines, [<i>].lines[<j>] in ascending string order (empty when it is not a list), checked after the game state's strategy block.
contract.conversationClockRule: Every timestamp in gameState.conversations and SaveFile.conversations[].recentTurns is the WALL-CLOCK UTC instant the host supplies, in Date.prototype.toISOString form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ: conversationTimestamp(epochMs) = that instant of floor(epochMs), null outside conversationMsRange or for a non-finite number. Never play time or game time dressed as an instant: play-time ms reads as a 1970 date on every other engine. A host that keeps play-time or game-time ms for its own history keeps the wall-clock instant too. The round trip back: conversationEpochMs(timestamp) = the epoch ms, or null unless the timestamp is in that form and writes back to itself (a missing ms part, another offset, a day the month lacks: null). The projection itself compares timestamps as strings and never parses them.
contract.skillKbRule: A load recomposes the skill KB (docs/progression-systems.md section 6): the skill pack, the world's program, the live facts, then the roster published over them; never the program composed when progression opened, and never the facts held before the load. A refused load changes nothing. skillKb = the checked read (any refusal is the load's), then: facts = currentState.prologFacts, each {predicate: an unquoted atom, args: [string with no control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F) or finite number]} as the clause the KB holds (an atom bare, any other string single-quoted with its quote and backslash escaped, a number as JavaScript writes it except that a mantissa with no fraction gets .0, so 1e-7 is 1.0e-7; no args: the bare atom), with a trailing period, once each, in ascending code-unit order; dropped = [{at: prologFacts[<i>], code}] in index order: skill_owned (a predicate in skillKbRosterPredicates: the progression block's; or a rule head the skill pack defines: can_advance/2, can_learn_skill/2, can_unlock/2, skill_capped/2, skill_effect/2, skill_goal_met/2, skill_node_price/2, skill_points_held/3, read from the pack's clauses, a live clause of which would be a clause added to the pack's rule; the same name at another arity is live), authored (one of the skill pack's authored predicates), reserved (a predicate in skillKbReservedPredicates: the shared engine owns it, so no skill KB can hold it), unreadable, duplicate (a clause already taken); prologFacts absent or null: no facts; not a list: [{at: prologFacts, code: unreadable}]; roster = what SkillProgression.publishActors asserts for currentState.extensions.progression.skills restored: actors by id, each its has_skill/3 by skill, skill_xp/3 by skill, skill_points/3 by tree, then skill_unlocked/2 in node order. In play, each fact the game asserts or retracts reaches the skill KB before the next skill decision (layered or recomposed; conformance/progression/skills.json op kb pins the answers).

skillKb: a fact the KB cannot hold is dropped and named: a predicate the engine owns (reserved), a control character (unreadable); an exponent number is written in Prolog's syntax (PL.core-skill-kb-live-facts)
cases.note: reserved: a predicate in contract.skillKbReservedPredicates, the shared engine's builtins, library predicates and hooks and the names whose clause no skill KB can hold (member/2, true/0, length/2, format/2; attribute/1, a prefix operator's name). member/3 is not the engine's, so it is live. unreadable: a string argument holding a control character. 1e-7 and 1e+21 are not Prolog numbers, so they are written 1.0e-7 and 1.0e+21.

cases.name: skillKb: a fact naming a rule head the skill pack defines is skill_owned; the same name at another arity is live (PL.core-skill-kb-rule-head-facts)
cases.note: skill_owned: can_advance/2, can_learn_skill/2, can_unlock/2, skill_capped/2, skill_effect/2, skill_goal_met/2, skill_node_price/2 and skill_points_held/3 are rule heads the skill pack defines, so a live clause of one would be a clause added to the pack's rule (a live can_unlock(player, guild_master) would be an answer the rule never gave). skill_goal_met/1, can_unlock/1 and skill_points_held/2 are other predicates, and load.
